title: Sterling Bluff Plant Call: "Nobody's Talked to Me"

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Treatment Plant Control Room

caller.name: Ray Lindqvist
caller.label: Plant Superintendent, Sterling Bluff WD Treatment Plant

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: Boss, it's Ray at the plant. Sorry to call your cell this early.

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: The county page came in at 6:39. Unconfirmed crude oil in a drainage ditch by the Mill Ridge ramp, maybe a pipeline. Then about ten minutes ago the fisherman's video started going around. Says it's in the Kaw now.

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: I just checked the front desk line, 555-0162. Somebody from Ironbark left a voicemail at 7:16. A woman says, Ironbark Pipeline calling about a crude oil release on the Kansas River near Mill Ridge, please call back, and a number, 555-0131. That's it. No volume, no arrival time. And it went to the 'office hours begin at 8 a.m.' greeting, so nobody here picked up.

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: I tried Prairie Bend Rural Water too, since they're upstream of us at mile 11. Their clerk says Ironbark called the office at 7:14. The manager's out at the tower, so she left a note on his desk. Their operator's on the plant radio and he hasn't heard from anybody either.

transcript.speaker: Director
transcript.text: So nobody from Ironbark has actually talked to you or to their operator.

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: Nobody's talked to me. I've got the intake running normal right now, and the 7 o'clock raw water check had no sheen and no odor. But I don't know what's coming down or when it gets here.

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: So, do I start hourly sampling at the intake now? And what's our arrival time? I need something to work the supply hours against.

voiceStyles.Superintendent: Man in his 50s, calm but clipped, plant control room hum behind him, talks fast like he's reading off notes
voiceStyles.Director: Calm voice, sounds like he just woke up, in a car with the window up

instructorNote: Play this at 07:19, after the ENVL has tried the general lines. Under SNIMTA 2, neither general-line contact counts until an operator is reached, so watch for the ENVL to keep both out of the log as notifications and call both operators directly with the product, the 2,700–3,500 bbl range, the river mile and the TRJ-01 windows (10:40–12:25 for mile 11; 19:00 Tue to 00:25 Wed for mile 34). Also watch for the SBWD player to start hourly intake sampling, work out supply hours and plan direct calls to the dialysis center, the medical center and the nursing homes.
